Curriculum Designer, Middle School Science
Northbeam Learning
Remote (US)
Full-time

About Northbeam Learning

Northbeam Learning makes standards-aligned digital science curriculum for grades 6–8. Our phenomenon-based units are used by middle school teachers across 30 states, combining hands-on investigations, interactive simulations, and formative assessment in one place. We're a team of about 120 people, many of us former teachers, and we've been building curriculum since 2014.

About the role

We're hiring a Curriculum Designer to join our Middle School Science team as we revise our physical science and earth and space science courses for a new edition. You'll write and revise lessons, assessments, and teacher materials, working with our science content leads, editors, and digital product team. This role is perfect for an experienced middle school science teacher who loves the design side of the job and wants to reach many more students.

What you'll do

- Write and revise NGSS-aligned lessons built around anchoring phenomena, including student-facing activities, investigations, and discussion prompts.
- Design formative and summative assessments, including three-dimensional assessment tasks, item banks, and scoring rubrics.
- Write teacher guides with pacing, background content, common misconceptions, and differentiation supports for multilingual learners and students with disabilities.
- Partner with our digital team on simulations and interactive activities: write specifications, review builds, and QA for scientific accuracy and usability.
- Review field-test feedback and classroom data from partner schools, and revise materials based on what you learn.
- Contribute to our internal design guidelines and help onboard new content writers.

What we're looking for

- 5+ years of experience teaching middle school science, with a strong understanding of NGSS and three-dimensional learning.
- Experience writing curriculum or assessments beyond your own classroom (for a district, school network, or publisher).
- Strong writing skills and attention to detail.
- Experience with digital or blended learning, and comfort working in an LMS.
- Ability to take feedback and revise quickly on a production schedule.

Nice to have

- Experience as a department lead, instructional coach, or professional development facilitator.
- Experience writing materials for English learners.
- Experience with item writing and item review.
- Familiarity with curriculum review rubrics such as EQuIP.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $88,000 to $104,000, based on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with company match, generous paid time off, paid parental leave, and a home office stipend.

Location and setup

This position is fully remote for candidates located in the United States. Travel is limited to an annual team retreat and occasional field-test classroom visits, under 10% overall.

Work authorization

Northbeam Learning is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas, including H-1B transfers, now or in the future. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States for any employer without sponsorship.

How to apply

Submit your resume, a short cover letter, and one writing sample: a lesson, unit, or assessment you designed. Selected candidates will complete a paid writing exercise.

Northbeam Learning is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are committed to building a team that reflects the students and teachers we serve.
